payload.keyword_data: DataForSEO Google Ads, Australia, 15 Nov 2026. No volume: 'how to brief a travel advisor', 'how to brief a travel agent', 'what to tell a travel agent', 'honeymoon travel agent', 'how to plan a honeymoon', 'honeymoon planning checklist'. Measured: 'how does a travel agent work' 30; 'questions to ask a travel agent' 10 (grouped with 'questions to ask travel agent', not additive); 'what to ask a travel agent' 10; 'how to use a travel agent' 10. 'honeymoon budget' and nine more variants not returned. About 60 a month across distinct 'travel agent' series. A practical spoke and conversion step to /travel, not a traffic play.

audience.notes: Couple fears adapted to the honeymoon. Fear A (couple fear 3, plus fear 1): 'spending a lot and still getting something generic', here a shortlist of the same five famous resorts every advisor sends, or perks that turn out to be optional. Fear B (couple fear 2, plus the 'minimal admin' goal): 'planning from the other side of the world with no one to call' and too much back and forth with busy careers; the brief should get a fitting proposal in one round and name who they call while away. Paying parent (advisory): if a parent is contributing to the honeymoon, the brief says who pays deposits and in what currency. Anti-persona: no 'cheap honeymoon', 'deal' or 'how to get upgrades for free' framing.

payload.search_intent: Informational with a practical deliverable: 'what do we tell an advisor so we get the right honeymoon'. Related searches ask for a sample, a template and a pdf. Current SERP serves advisors (trade content), not travellers.
payload.angle: A good brief is the difference between a shortlist that fits and three rounds of 'not quite'. Agree five things as a couple, tell the advisor the details that actually change the shortlist, cover the days between the wedding and the honeymoon that most couples forget, ask the questions that get answers in writing, then copy the brief template and send it. Answer the search in the first 60 words.
serp_gaps_to_win: No consumer guide ranks for the head term in any city; page one is trade content for advisors plus social posts. A copyable brief template answers the 'sample / template / pdf' related searches no one serves.
The handover from wedding to honeymoon: checkout, onward flight, wedding attire and luggage, a rest day, documents in the right name. None of the 'how to plan a honeymoon' results covers it.

What to tell an advisor that actually changes the shortlist (budget range and what it includes, pace, suite priorities, past hotels loved and disliked, deal-breakers), not 'choose a destination you both enjoy'.
Questions to ask back so inclusions and terms come in writing, written for luxury travellers (Australian, AUD).
Australian content: every ranking 'how to plan a honeymoon' page is US, UK, Irish or Indian, dated 2016 to 2025.

outline.h2: What a good honeymoon brief does
outline.answers: The search itself, in the first 60 words: what to give a travel advisor so the first proposal fits.
must_include: Opening answer (under 60 words): a good brief tells the advisor your dates, a budget range and what it covers, the pace and style you want, your must-haves and deal-breakers, and how the honeymoon connects to the wedding. With that, the first proposal should be close; without it, expect rounds of revisions.
Key takeaways block (3 to 5 specific sentences) right after the intro.
First link to /travel within 150 words, descriptive anchor (e.g. 'how our travel team plans honeymoons alongside the wedding').
One sentence linking up to the parent (conditional, see internal_links_planned) for readers still deciding whether to use an advisor at all. Do not summarise the parent.

outline.h2: Agree these five things as a couple first
outline.answers: What do we need to decide before we contact anyone?
must_include: Five decisions: dates and length; a total budget range and what it includes (flights or not, cabin class); pace (one place or two or three stops, active or slow); the non-negotiables for each of you; what you would happily skip.
Each with one line on why it changes the shortlist (e.g. two stops in ten days means a transfer day lost).

Links: /expert-advice/how-long-is-a-honeymoon-a-guide-by-destination (length), /expert-advice/luxury-honeymoon-budget-which-destination-suits-yours (budget range). Optional: one /expert-advice/a-guide-on-where-to-go-on-honeymoon-in-<month> page if the text uses that month as an example.
No budget figures, no destination prices. Say 'a range you are both comfortable with'.

outline.h2: What to tell a travel agent: the details that change the shortlist
outline.answers: What details matter most to an advisor? ('what to tell a travel agent').
must_include: Room and suite priorities (view, private pool, size, villa vs hotel), with a note that suite category drives cost more than almost anything else (only if research or the honeymoon page supports it; otherwise drop the comparison).
Hotels you loved and hated before, and why: the fastest way to show taste.
The occasion: say it is a honeymoon and give the wedding date.
Dietary needs, accessibility, health, and anything that rules out long transfers, boats or altitude.
Loyalty memberships and points you want used (no claim about what they earn).
What you do not want (a short list of deal-breakers): one line only, no copying of the social post in the SERP.
Who is paying and how: if a parent or family is contributing, say who holds the booking and pays deposits (paying_parent).

outline.h2: The days between the wedding and the honeymoon
outline.answers: The invisible work: what couples forget to brief.
must_include: Checkout from the wedding property and the onward flight or transfer: give the advisor the wedding venue, the last event and the morning you can realistically leave.
A rest day or a late start before a long flight; whether to leave straight away or later (link /expert-advice/a-guide-on-when-to-go-on-honeymoon).
Wedding attire and extra luggage: who takes the dress and suits home, or whether storage or shipping is needed (no supplier names).

Documents: book travel in the name on your passport; if either of you plans to change names, do it after travel or check first. Visa and entry rules and travel insurance from Smartraveller only (research). No legal advice.

If the wedding is abroad: same advisor and one booking record across wedding and honeymoon (brand wording from research A: 'one connected journey', 'one specialist coordinating the whole trip'). One sentence; the parent owns the detail.

outline.h2: Questions to ask your advisor before you say yes
outline.answers: What should we ask back? ('questions to ask a travel agent').
must_include: Which inclusions are confirmed in writing per booking, and which are requests or 'subject to availability' (upgrades, late checkout). Use /travel wording only (research A).
Payment schedule, deposit amounts and dates, the currency you will be charged in.
Cancellation and change terms for each hotel and flight; travel insurance cover start date (Smartraveller).
Who we call while we are away, and the hours that number answers.
What happens to the plan if the wedding date moves.
Do NOT include: how advisors are paid, commission, fees, ATAS, ACCC consumer guarantees. One sentence linking to the parent's section instead (conditional).

outline.answers: Give me something I can copy and send.
must_include: A copyable block (plain text, fenced or styled as a card) with fill-in fields: Names and contact; Wedding date and location; Honeymoon dates (fixed or flexible by how many days); Departure city; Length; Budget range in AUD and what it includes (flights yes/no, cabin class); Destinations considered or ruled out; Pace (one stop / two stops); Room priorities; Must-haves (each of us); Deal-breakers; Hotels we loved and why; Hotels we did not and why; Dietary, health, accessibility; Loyalty programs; Special moments (a dinner, an experience); Who is paying and deposit contact; Passport names match bookings (yes/no); Best way and times to reach us.
Short note: send it with three or four photos or links of places you love; ask for a shortlist of two or three, not ten.
Optional: offer the template as a downloadable PDF later (answers the 'pdf' related search). Flag as an open question; do not promise a download in copy.

outline.answers: How do we start with you, and how far ahead?
must_include: The live process only (research A): the 'Start planning' form on /travel takes dates and destination and the team replies with a shortlist, rates and inclusions; scope can be hotel only, guest travel, honeymoon or all of it; any planning fee is disclosed before work starts (quote /travel wording, no figure).
Lead time: our honeymoon page suggests six to nine months to secure the right suite category (research A wording).
Link /destination-honeymoon-packages with a descriptive anchor (e.g. 'what our honeymoon specialists include'), not 'honeymoon packages'. Do not list its inclusions.
One line for couples also planning the wedding: the Discovery Call covers travel and accommodation needs (soft discovery_call line, links /wonderland-concierge).
One line on /wedded-world (no ticket push), only if it fits naturally; otherwise omit.
Closing CTA block: travel_benefits.

faq: How far ahead should we brief a travel advisor for our honeymoon?
How much should we budget for a honeymoon?
Is there a downside to using a travel agent?
payload.faq_note: Six max, all from PAA. Q1 adapts 'How to plan for a honeymoon?' (all three cities); answer with the honeymoon page's six to nine months. Q2 adapts 'How much money to save for a honeymoon?' and 'Is $5000 enough for a honeymoon?': no figures; tell the advisor a range and what it covers; link the luxury honeymoon budget article. Q3 and Q4 from PAA (all three cities): define briefly and say how each changes the brief (two trips; friends joining means more rooms and a group booking). Definitions from research or general usage, no invented stats. Q5 adapts 'Who is responsible for paying for a honeymoon?': tradition varies, today usually the couple, sometimes family or a registry; tell your advisor who pays deposits (paying_parent). Q6 from the head-term PAA: honest answer (a vague brief wastes rounds; ask how they are paid) with a link to the parent's payment section instead of repeating it. Excluded PAA: 'How to write a travel guide?', 'Is it hard to be a travel advisor?', 'How much does a travel agent make on a $10,000 trip?' (trade or owned by the parent), 'Is it actually cheaper to use a travel agent?' (parent).
must_include: Direct answer to 'how to brief a travel advisor' in the first 60 words.
Fear A (generic result): the 'details that change the shortlist' H2 and hotels loved and hated; inclusions confirmed in writing.
Fear B (no one to call, minimal admin): one-round brief, 'who we call while away' question, one booking record across wedding and honeymoon.
Paying parent: who pays deposits and in what currency, in the details H2, the questions H2 and the template.
Invisible work H2: the days between the wedding and the honeymoon, documents in passport names, attire and luggage.
Copyable brief template.
Brand facts only from research A (the parent's pack, live /travel and honeymoon page wording) or brand-profile.md. Travel facts (visas, entry, insurance, names on tickets) from Smartraveller only.
Key takeaways block, soft discovery_call line, closing travel_benefits CTA. Australian English, AUD.
must_avoid: Repeating the parent: how advisors are paid, commission, the /travel fee line beyond one quoted clause, ATAS, ACCC consumer guarantees, room blocks, 'travel advisor vs travel agent' definitions, the 'who does what' table.
Destination prices, budget figures, the honeymoon page's US$ price range, invented itineraries, 'secret' or 'insider' perks.
Guaranteed upgrades or late checkout; 'free', 'cheap', 'deal', 'discount', 'stress-free', 'hassle-free', 'dream honeymoon'.
Naming or linking ranking agencies, tour operators, social accounts or trade sites (domains.md).

Exact-match anchors owned by other pages: 'travel advisor wedding', 'wedding travel advisor', 'honeymoon packages', 'luxury honeymoon budget', 'when to go on honeymoon', 'how long is a honeymoon'. Also not 'honeymoon travel' or 'wedding travel' as a bare anchor to /travel.
Linking the two legacy honeymoon posts (not in link-map).
Em dashes and banned style-guide words.
payload.word_count_note: Range set by the orchestrator. No meaningful competitor median (snippets only; listicles in the honeymoon SERP look short). Aim near 1,700; the template and the questions list carry the length. Do not pad.

cta.soft: discovery_call (one line in the last H2, for couples also planning the wedding)
cta.soft_line: If you are planning the wedding as well, a free Discovery Call with a Wedded Wonderland advisor covers travel and accommodation needs too.
cta.why: travel_benefits closes because the reader of this spoke has already decided to use an advisor and is holding a finished brief; the next action is to send it, and /travel is where the 'Start planning' form lives. Its body (partner-property benefits, varying by hotel and program) also matches the 'confirmed in writing' question. discovery_call is the parent's closing CTA and fits a reader still deciding; here it would add a step between a ready brief and the form, so it drops to a soft line for couples planning the wedding too.

internal_links_planned.note: Required, at least twice: intro and last H2 (plus the CTA block). Descriptive anchors, e.g. 'how our travel team plans honeymoons alongside the wedding', 'send your brief through our travel page'.

payload.cannibalisation_verdict: No page owns 'how to brief a travel advisor', 'what to tell a travel agent' or 'questions to ask a travel agent'. Write the article as a spoke; keep the parent's pay and accreditation material out.
payload.differentiation: Parent: what an advisor does, is it worth it, how they are paid, who does what. Section 8 articles: how much, when, how long, where. This spoke: how to turn those decisions into a brief an advisor can act on in one round, what to ask back, and a template to send.

research_asks.note: One research batch is running in parallel; this list is for coverage cross-checking only. Strategist has not researched facts.
brand_reuse_from_parent_research_A: /travel: 'Start planning' form (dates and destination; reply with shortlist, rates and inclusions); scope wording ('Hotel only, the full celebration week, guest travel, honeymoon or all of it'); 'If any planning fee applies, you know before we start'; 'one connected journey'; 'we stay reachable while you are away'; perks as requests vs confirmed.
/destination-honeymoon-packages: 6 to 9 months lead time wording; 'one specialist coordinating the whole trip'. No price range.
/wonderland-concierge: Discovery Call covers 'Travel and accommodation needs'; step 06 'Travel & Honeymoon Concierge'.
smartraveller_only: Book tickets in the name on your passport; changing names after marriage and travel documents (Smartraveller or Australian Passport Office).
Check visa and entry requirements per destination; passport validity guidance.
Travel insurance: when to buy, what to check (pre-existing conditions, cancellation cover).
Optional: definitions for 'mini honeymoon' and 'buddymoon' if an authoritative or editorial source is quick; otherwise plain-language definitions with no statistics.
